```{r clean-function}
clean_pums <- function(df) {
  df |>
    select(SERIALNO, SPORDER, PERNP_adj, any_of(predictor_vars)) |>
    mutate(
      STATE = factor(STATE, levels = names(state_lookup),
                    labels = unname(state_lookup)),
      SEX = factor(SEX, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Male", "Female")),
      RAC1P = factor(RAC1P, levels = names(rac1p_lookup),
                    labels = unname(rac1p_lookup)),
      MAR = factor(MAR, levels = names(mar_lookup),
                    labels = unname(mar_lookup)),
      PAOC = factor(coalesce(PAOC, "N"),
                    levels = names(paoc_lookup),
                    labels = unname(paoc_lookup)),
      CIT = factor(CIT, levels = names(cit_lookup),
                    labels = unname(cit_lookup)),
      NATIVITY = factor(NATIVITY, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Native", "Foreign Born")),
      LANX = factor(LANX, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Speaks another Language", "Only English")),
      ENG = factor(coalesce(ENG, "N"),
                    levels = names(eng_lookup),
                    labels = unname(eng_lookup)),
      WAOB = factor(WAOB, levels = names(waob_lookup),
                    labels = unname(waob_lookup)),
      DIS = factor(DIS, levels = 1:2, labels = c("With a Disability", "Without a Disability")),
      DRAT = factor(coalesce(DRAT, "N"),
                    levels = names(drat_lookup),
                    labels = unname(drat_lookup)),
      SCIENGRLP = factor(coalesce(SCIENGRLP, "N"),
                    levels = names(sciengrlp_lookup),
                    labels = unname(sciengrlp_lookup)),
      FOD1P = factor(coalesce(FOD1P, "N"),
                    levels = names(fod1p_lookup),
                    labels = unname(fod1p_lookup)),
      

      across(c(DRATX, DEAR, DEYE, DPHY, DREM, DDRS, DOUT),
             ~ factor(.x, levels = c("1", "2"), labels = c("Yes", "No")))  
    )
}

dev <- clean_pums(dev_raw)
glimpse(dev)
```

zero? negatives? skew? top-coding?) because they affect your metric and
modeling choices in Section 6.

```{r outcome-dist}
dev |>
```

## 5(e) Missing data

PUMS uses blank/NA for "not applicable," which is not the same as "missing at
random." Read the dictionary for each predictor to learn what NA means
(e.g., N/A because of age vs. truly unreported).

```{r missing}
dev |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "n_na") |>
  mutate(prop_na = n_na / nrow(dev)) |>
  arrange(desc(n_na))
```

```{r folds}
folds
```

Preprocessing lives inside `recipe()`s so it is re-fit on the analysis portion
of each fold and applied to that fold's assessment portion.

## 6(c) Baseline

```{r baseline}
# Predict the training-fold mean income. Evaluated on the same folds.
baseline_spec <- null_model() |> set_engine("parsnip") |> set_mode("regression")

baseline_res <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(income ~ 1) |>
  add_model(baseline_spec) |>
  fit_resamples(folds, metrics = my_metrics)

collect_metrics(baseline_res)
```

## 6(d) Algorithms and feature sets

Feature sets: define at least two, apply to EVERY algorithm. Use exploration
findings to motivate them. Keep them as *formulas or recipe steps* so they are
reusable.

```{r feature-sets}
# TODO: define your two (or more) feature sets and the rationale for each.
# Examples of differences: with/without a group of variables, collapsed vs
# full-granularity categories, added interactions or nonlinear terms
# (e.g., age^2), engineered features.

# Shared preprocessing skeleton: recipe is fit on training portion of each fold
make_recipe <- function(formula, data = dev) {
  recipe(formula, data = data) |>
    update_role(SERIALNO, SPORDER, new_role = "id") |>   # keep IDs out of the model
    step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>      # TODO: your missing-data plan
    step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_other(all_nominal_predictors(), threshold = 0.01) |>  # TODO: justify threshold
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())             # needed for lasso; harmless for OLS/trees
}
# NOTE: if you use ID columns, include them in the formula so the roles apply,
# e.g. income ~ . but then drop outcome-leaking columns explicitly.

fs_A <- income ~ AGEP + SEX + RAC1P + SCHL + SERIALNO + SPORDER               # TODO: smaller set
fs_B <- income ~ AGEP + SEX + RAC1P + SCHL + MAR + DIS + HISP + ST + SERIALNO + SPORDER  # TODO: richer set

feature_sets <- list(A = fs_A, B = fs_B)
```

Algorithms (at least three; at least one non-linear-model-family):

```{r algorithms}
# TODO: for each, write 2-3 sentences in your report on why you chose it and
# how it produces predictions. You must be able to explain tuning parameters.

lin_spec <- linear_reg() |> set_engine("lm")                       # linear regression (required)

lasso_spec <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) |>         # linear-family, but remember it
  set_engine("glmnet")                                             # doesn't count as "non-linear"

rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>  # non-linear family
  set_mode("regression") |>
  set_engine("ranger")

# Alternatives for the third algorithm: decision tree (rpart), boosted trees
# (xgboost), kNN, etc. Pick what you can explain and defend.
```

## 6(e) Train, tune, compare

```{r tuning-grids}
# Document the scope of search for the report (number of trials/grid size).
lasso_grid <- grid_regular(penalty(range = c(-4, 0)), levels = 20)   # TODO: justify range

rf_grid_fn <- function(rec) {
  # mtry upper bound depends on the number of predictors after the recipe
  n_pred <- rec |> prep(dev) |> bake(new_data = NULL) |>
    select(-any_of(c("income", "SERIALNO", "SPORDER"))) |> ncol()
  grid_regular(mtry(range = c(1, n_pred)), min_n(range = c(5, 50)), levels = 4)  # TODO
}
```

```{r run-experiments}
run_one <- function(spec, formula, grid = NULL, fs_name, algo_name) {
  rec <- make_recipe(formula)
  wf  <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec) |> add_model(spec)

  if (is.null(grid)) {
    res <- fit_resamples(wf, folds, metrics = my_metrics)
  } else {
    set.seed(GLOBAL_SEED)   # same seed for every tuning run
    res <- tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid, metrics = my_metrics)
  }
  list(res = res, wf = wf, fs = fs_name, algo = algo_name,
       n_configs = if (is.null(grid)) 1 else nrow(grid))
}

results <- list()
for (fs_name in names(feature_sets)) {
  f <- feature_sets[[fs_name]]
  results[[paste("lm",    fs_name)]] <- run_one(lin_spec,   f, NULL,       fs_name, "Linear regression")
  results[[paste("lasso", fs_name)]] <- run_one(lasso_spec, f, lasso_grid, fs_name, "Lasso")
  results[[paste("rf",    fs_name)]] <- run_one(rf_spec,    f,
                                                 rf_grid_fn(make_recipe(f)), fs_name, "Random forest")
}
```

Comparison table (one table for the report: add the baseline row, and tuning
settings tried / selected):

```{r comparison-table}
best_row <- function(x) {
  m <- collect_metrics(x$res) |> filter(.metric == primary_metric)
  m |> slice_min(mean, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(algorithm = x$algo, feature_set = x$fs, n_configs = x$n_configs)
}

comparison <- map(results, best_row) |> list_rbind() |>
  select(algorithm, feature_set, n_configs, mean, std_err, any_of(c("penalty", "mtry", "min_n"))) |>
  arrange(mean)

baseline_row <- collect_metrics(baseline_res) |>
  filter(.metric == primary_metric) |>
  transmute(algorithm = "Baseline (mean)", feature_set = "-", n_configs = 1, mean, std_err)

bind_rows(baseline_row, comparison) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## 6(f) Final model selection and saved pipeline

```{r final-model}
# TODO: choose the winner by your primary metric (and explain/interpret it).
winner_key <- comparison |> slice(1)
winner <- results[[ paste(c("Linear regression" = "lm", "Lasso" = "lasso",
                            "Random forest" = "rf")[winner_key$algorithm],
                          winner_key$feature_set) ]]

best_params <- if (winner$n_configs > 1) select_best(winner$res, metric = primary_metric) else NULL

final_wf <- if (!is.null(best_params)) finalize_workflow(winner$wf, best_params) else winner$wf

# Refit on ALL development data (allowed by the handout); recipe is re-fit here too
final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = dev)

# Save everything needed to predict in Part 2:
# fitted workflow (includes fitted recipe + model), cleaning function, metadata
dir.create("final_pipeline", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(final_fit, "final_pipeline/final_fit.rds")
saveRDS(list(
  clean_pums     = clean_pums,
  predictor_vars = predictor_vars,
  best_params    = best_params,
  primary_metric = primary_metric,
  seed           = GLOBAL_SEED,
  algorithm      = winner_key$algorithm,
  feature_set    = winner_key$feature_set
), "final_pipeline/pipeline_meta.rds")

# Interpretation helpers (pick what fits your model):
# - lm/lasso: tidy(extract_fit_parsnip(final_fit))
# - rf: vip::vip(extract_fit_parsnip(final_fit)) or permutation importance
```
